in_arabic.name: محجّد
in_arabic.long_meaning: المُحجّد هو الّذي يُشجّع ويُثبت في الإسلام، حيثُ يُشجّع المؤمنين على الطّاعة والعمل الصّالح، ويُثبت في قلوبهم الإيمان واليقين، ويعزّزهم في سبيل الله، ويُحفظهم من الأذى والخطر.

in_urdu.name: مُحجّد
in_urdu.meaning: وہ جو نیک کام کرتا ہے اور لوگوں کو بھی اچھا کام کرنے پر مائل کرتا ہے
in_urdu.long_meaning: مُحجّد ایک اسلامی نام ہے جس کا مطلب ہے وہ جو نیک کام کرتا ہے اور لوگوں کو بھی اچھا کام کرنے پر مائل کرتا ہے۔ اس نام کی اہمیت اس لیے ہے کہ یہ مسلمانوں کو نیک اعمال پر مائل کرنے اور اللہ تعالیٰ کی راہ میں کھڑے ہونے کا پیغام دیتا ہے۔

in_hindi.name: मुख़जद
in_hindi.meaning: वह जो अच्छा काम करता है और दूसरों को भी अच्छा काम करने के लिए प्रोत्साहित करता है
in_hindi.long_meaning: मुख़जद एक इस्लामी नाम है जिसका अर्थ है वह जो अच्छा काम करता है और दूसरों को भी अच्छा काम करने के लिए प्रोत्साहित करता है। इस नाम का महत्व इसलिए है कि यह मुस्लिमों को अच्छे कामों पर मोहित करने और अल्लाह की राह पर खड़े रहने का संदेश देता है।

in_english.name: Muhjid
in_english.meaning: The one who encourages and promotes good deeds, and inspires others to do the same
in_english.long_meaning: Muhjid is an Islamic name that means The one who encourages and promotes good deeds, and inspires others to do the same. This name has great importance in Islamic tradition as it motivates Muslims to perform good actions and encourages others to follow suit. The root of the name is derived from the Arabic word 'mujadda,' which means to encourage or promote. In Islamic context, Muhjid is a name that symbolizes the qualities of a good Muslim, who strives to do good deeds and inspires others to do the same. The name Muhjid is a reminder of the importance of promoting good actions and encouraging others to follow the right path.

data.cultural_impact: The name Muhjid holds great significance in Islamic culture and the Arabic language as it signifies an individual who is deeply committed to fighting for a righteous cause, often in the face of adversity and hardship. Historically, it has been used to describe great warriors, freedom fighters, and scholars. For example, during the time of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), those who went to defend and spread Islam to new lands were known as Muhjidin (plural of Muhjid).
data.spiritual_significance: To bear the mantle of a Muhjid, spiritually, carries the weight of being a servant of Allah, striving in His cause with utmost sincerity, determination, and perseverance. A true Muhjid recognizes that this journey is not about worldly gains but about pleasing their Creator, seeking His ultimate reward in both this world and the next. As well, the spiritual significance extends beyond physical warfare, as the process of internal struggle, self-discipline, and moral growth is also an essential part of being a Muhjid.

islamic_reference.note: Traditional Islamic name with deep spiritual significance in Islamic culture

historical_references.reference: The title 'Muhjid' was given to the Prophet Muhammad's companions who migrated from Mecca to Medina to escape persecution. This migration, known as the Hijra, took place in 622 AD. Muhjid means 'struggler in the way of Allah'.
historical_references.context: The Prophet Muhammad and his followers were facing intense persecution in Mecca. In order to safely establish a Muslim community and spread the message of Islam, they migrated to the city of Medina. The companions who made this journey were known as Muhjid (strugglers) because they were leaving behind their homes, families, and livelihoods to face the challenges of establishing a new community in a foreign land and spreading the message of Islam.

historical_references.reference: During the early Islamic period, the title 'Muhjid' was also given to warriors who fought in the cause of Allah. These soldiers were known as 'Mujahideen' and their military campaigns were known as 'jihad'. The term Muhjid thus came to signify anyone who made a strenuous effort in the way of Allah, whether through physical struggle or spiritual endeavor.
historical_references.context: The Islamic conquests expanded rapidly during this period, and the Islamic state came into conflict with various non-Muslim powers. The Islamic community needed soldiers to defend its borders and expand its territory. These soldiers were known as Mujahideen, or 'strugglers in the way of Allah'. The term Muhjid thus came to signify anyone who made a strenuous effort in the way of Allah, whether through military struggle or spiritual endeavor.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Muhjid' in Islamic context refers to a person who strives to spread knowledge and guidance in the path of righteousness. In today's digital age, this name is embraced by individuals who use various online platforms to inspire, educate and empower others. On Instagram, Muhjids share motivational quotes, spiritual art, and inspirational stories to encourage personal growth and self-improvement. On YouTube, they create content focused on teaching Islamic principles, providing Islamic counseling, and conducting live Quran recitations. On Medium, they publish articles and essays on Islamic spirituality, contemporary issues, and personal experiences. Overall, the modern Muhjid is a spiritual guide, a source of knowledge, and an inspiration for personal growth and self-empowerment.
